intent: An in-place combat-stance running cycle: the legs alternately lift, extend, and take load; the upper body rotates with the rhythm, while both arms remain bent and asymmetric rather than swinging freely.

phases.description: The left knee drives upward while the right leg trails; the hips rise toward the first apex.
The left leg extends downward, then the body drops into left-side loading/compression while the right leg folds back.
The right knee drives upward while the left leg trails; the hips rise toward the second apex.
The right leg extends downward, then the body drops into right-side loading/compression while the left leg folds back.
The cycle closes back to f0.

weightTransfer: Weight alternates to the left during f5-f9 and to the right during f15-f20; the hips clearly lower after each lead-leg extension as the body moves into loading/compression. These loading points are inferred from leg configuration and hip variation, not from a contact channel.
bodyMechanics: The mechanical sequence repeats side to side: lead knee lift -> lead leg extends downward -> hips lower/compress -> opposite leg folds back -> side switch. The upper body rotates through the cycle, while both arms remain bent and asymmetric instead of swinging symmetrically as in neutral running. The clip is named `sword-and-shield-run`, but the preview does not render sword or shield meshes, so the evidence supports only a combat-running posture with bent/asymmetric arms rather than explicit sword/shield mechanics.

recommended: Leg and hip rhythm for a weapon-carrying character.
Running with a compact, asymmetric upper-body carriage.
notRecommended: Neutral running with free arm swing.
Motion with root translation through world space.
Exact sword or shield mechanics because the preview does not render sword/shield meshes.
Exact support-foot or ground-contact identification because the data has no ground/contact marker.
